title: Adaptive POP chooser: dual-quantile latency + path-quality arbiter with tiered-fallbacks
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: implement an adaptive POP (point-of-presence) selection arbiter that fuses latency quantiles (p50 and p95) with a compact path-quality network health score to pick region/tier and trigger graceful fallback to compatible model variants. This ticket covers: metric fusion algorithm, hysteresis/smoothing, tier preference policy (hosted -> dedicated -> private based on SLA and cost rules), variant compatibility matrix and a deployable feature flag with rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New arbiter returns a ranked list of up to 3 POPs for each request with a deterministic tiebreaker.
2) Ranking is computed from fused score combining p50, p95 and network health (packet loss + retransmit rate + recent infra errors).
3) End-to-end median latency (p50) for synthetic cross-region test harness must improve on unstable POPs vs baseline routing by >= 15% for affected cohorts while p95 regression is <= 3%.
4) When primary POP score drops below threshold, system falls back to next POP and optionally routes to a lower-cost quantized model variant; fallbacks must preserve model API contract and tokenization.
5) Feature flag allows canary on 5% of traffic, with automatic rollback if error-rate increases by >2x or p95 increases by >20%.
6) Unit tests + integration tests (simulated network faults) exist and pass in CI.
updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff sync with product and console teams. Agreed on target SLOs and rollout constraints.
2025-02-18: Prototype dual-quantile fusion computed locally using EWMA for short-term smoothing; initial thresholds proposed (p50_threshold_ms=80, p95_threshold_ms=220).

2025-02-22: Design review with Runtime and Networking. Decided to include path-quality score combining packet_loss(1m), tcp_retransmit_rate(1m), and APICallErrors(5m) weighted as [0.5,0.3,0.2] respectively.
2025-02-28: Implemented scoring library and unit tests. Began integration into request router; end-to-end tests in staging scheduled week of 2025-03-03.
2025-03-02: PM requested additional opt-in to allow forcing variant-only fallbacks for enterprise customers. Added as config flag in plan.
notes:priority-decisions: use smoothing-window 60s EWMA for p50, 120s for p95 to avoid oscillation on transient spikes.
telemetry_queries:
-- p50/p95 per-pop over last 5m
SELECT pop, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) AS p50, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) AS p95 FROM request_spans WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '5 minutes' GROUP BY pop;

-- path quality: packet loss, retransmit, infra errors (1m)
SELECT pop, avg(packet_loss_pct) AS pkt_loss, avg(tcp_retransmit_rate) AS retransmit, sum(infra_errors) AS errors FROM network_metrics WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '1 minute' GROUP BY pop;

-- fused score computation for analysis
WITH latency AS ( /* p50/p95 */ ), path AS ( /* pktloss/retransmit */ ) SELECT pop, (w1 * normalized_p95 + w2 * normalized_p50 + w3 * normalized_path) AS fused_score FROM ...;
technical_decisions:
1) Fusion formula: fused_score = alpha * z(p95) + beta * z(p50) + gamma * z(path_health) where z() is z-score normalized per-pop over a rolling baseline; alpha=0.5, beta=0.25, gamma=0.25. We normalize to reduce bias from pops with different baselines.
2) Smoothing: EWMA with separate half-lives for p50 (60s) and p95 (120s).
3) Hysteresis: require sustained violation for 30s before demoting a POP; once demoted enforce cooldown of 2 minutes.
4) Tier routing policy: prefer dedicated instances for enterprise-marked requests, but if fused_score of dedicated POP is > fail_threshold then route to hosted POP or next-best private POP.
5) Fallback variant rules: allow model variant downgrade only if the request's model_schema is compatible (same tokenizer + output schema) and variants are declared in compatibility matrix in model catalog.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary 5%): enable arbiter for internal and low-risk tenants, collect metrics for 72h. Phase 2 (30%): expand to regular tenants and run A/B comparison vs current routing for 7 days. Phase 3 (100%): global rollout with monitoring alerts. Automated rollback triggers: >2x error rate, p95 increase >20%, or >10% of requests seeing fallback variant within 5m window.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring library, integration harness simulating network degradation (packet drops, increased RTT, control-plane errors). Load test with synthetic clients across regions to validate no regression in throughput. Create chaos-testing job to randomly blackhole a POP and assert graceful fallback within <1s for in-flight requests and <200ms for new requests routing decision time.
risks:
1) Over-reactive routing: oscillations causing request churn between POPs. Mitigation: EWMA smoothing, hysteresis and cooldown.
2) Variant mismatches leading to subtle behavior changes for customers: Mitigation: strict compatibility checks and opt-in for enterprise tenants.
3) Telemetry skew: incomplete or delayed metrics may bias score. Mitigation: fall back to historical baseline when telemetry is stale and surface a 'telemetry_stale' flag in routing decisions.
